summary: This document details the architecture and implementation of Strada, a private networking tracker application. It emphasizes that data ownership and security are enforced primarily by Postgres Row Level Security (RLS), with the Express API acting as a controlled gateway. The application uses Neon Postgres and Managed Better Auth to ensure that each user can only interact with their own private contact data.
key_facts: The application uses React 19, Vite, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4 for the Frontend.
The Backend is Express 5 + TypeScript (ESM) and deployed as a separate Vercel project.
Neon Postgres is used for the database, with RLS policies enforced on the contacts table.
Authentication uses Neon Managed Better Auth and issues Ed25519 JWTs with a lifetime of 900 seconds.
The Express layer never connects to Postgres; it forwards the caller's own token to the Neon Data API.
The `contacts` table includes columns like `name`, `company`, `role`, `met_where`, `notes`, and `priority`.
The application includes 163 hermetic tests and 25 live RLS proof tests.
The design ensures that the database, not the API server, enforces ownership and security boundaries.

concepts.name: Row Level Security
concepts.definition: A database feature that restricts which rows a user can see or modify.
concepts.in_this_source: RLS policies are used to enforce that each user can only interact with their own private contact data.

concepts.name: Managed Better Auth
concepts.definition: An authentication service that issues JWTs and manages user sessions.
concepts.in_this_source: Neon Managed Better Auth issues Ed25519 JWTs whose `sub` claim is read by Postgres to determine ownership.

concepts.name: Neon Postgres
concepts.in_this_source: Neon Postgres hosts the contacts table and executes all RLS policies and CHECK constraints.

concepts.name: Vercel
concepts.definition: A cloud platform used for deploying web applications.
concepts.in_this_source: Vercel hosts both the Frontend (Project A) and the Backend API (Project B).

concepts.name: Express
concepts.definition: A minimal and flexible Node.js web application framework.
concepts.in_this_source: Express serves as the small, explicit HTTP layer between the frontend and the Data API.
